Change c0534. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. VII; 1831 Ch. XXIV.

Context before (unchanged): I, who irretrievably destroyed thee by destroying all thou lovedst.

1818 text: Alas! he is cold; he may not answer me."

1831 text: Alas! he is cold, he cannot answer me."

Diff: Alas! he is cold [-;-] {+,+} he [-may not-] {+cannot+} answer me. "

Context after (unchanged): His voice seemed suffocated; and my first impulses, which had suggested to me the duty of obeying the dying request of my friend, in destroying his enemy, were now suspended by a mixture of curiosity and compassion.

result.rationale: Punctuation change from semicolon to comma and replacement of 'may not' with 'cannot' alters modal nuance from permission/possibility to inability, while keeping the same meaning in the Creature's lament over Victor's body.
